**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 3 of 7 (format / tooltip / meta / detail).

## Target outcome

Row formatting, the hover tooltip, the metadata panel (rows, preview cache,
content height) and the detail view (ToC, content, file viewer, note-edit
write-back, key-file resolution) each live in a named module, so a change to one
surface produces a diff attributable to one module.

## Scope (measured line ranges)

| New module | Contents | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.format.ts` | `formatItemLine` (1357–1609), `formatTimestamp` (1610–1620), plus the module-local width/pad/highlight helpers at 1326–1356 | ~300 |
| `worklist.tooltip.ts` | `formatTooltipLines` (1637–1707), `formatTooltipOverlay` (1708–1746) | ~130 |
| `worklist.meta.ts` | `buildMetaRows` (1747–1858), `pairMetaRows` (1887–1920), description preview cache (1922–1952, incl. `clearDescriptionPreviewCache`), metadata panel body (1953–2114), `metadataPanelContentHeight` (2115–2150), `formatMetadataPanel` (2151–2208), `resolveMetaLastCommand` (2209–2232), `formatGroupInfoPanel` (2233–2279) | ~640 |

Note: `buildMetaRows` physically sits inside the "Hover tooltip rendering"
banner range but is a metadata-row builder shared by the metadata panel and the
detail view — it moves to `worklist.meta.ts` (with the
`// ── Compound metadata rows (WL-0MSNIX4V60012266) ──` provenance). The
`// ── Hover tooltip rendering (WL-0MT9XRZDK006GMUH) ──`,
`// ── Description preview cache (WL-0MT9ZJF28004UJ28) ──` and
`// ── Note-edit write-back (WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR) ──` banners move with their code.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The four modules exist, each ≤1,000 lines, each with a responsibility doc
   comment; provenance banners and inline work-item ids move verbatim (AC6).
2. The description preview cache remains a single module-level instance with the
   same invalidation semantics (one declaration, not duplicated per view) —
   `formatMetadataPanel` and `formatDetailContent` keep reading the same cache
   and the same `buildMetaRows`/`pairMetaRows` implementation (no behavioural
   fork; recorded in the completion comment).
3. The barrel re-exports exactly the consumed symbols in this slice:
   `formatItemLine`, `formatTimestamp`, `formatTooltipLines`,
   `formatTooltipOverlay`, `buildMetaRows`, `pairMetaRows`,
   `formatMetadataPanel`, `metadataPanelContentHeight`,
   `resolveMetaLastCommand`, `formatGroupInfoPanel`,
   `clearDescriptionPreviewCache`, `formatDetailContent`, `renderFileViewer`,
   `formatDetailView`, `firstMarkdownKeyFile`, `resolveKeyFilePath`.
   **Internal** (no external consumer imports them): `formatDetailToC`,
   `formatFilterPrompt`.
   *(Plan-time correction, 2026-10-30: the guarded symbol set is re-derived
from the live import scan — 66 symbols are imported by the 36 consumer
files. Every symbol listed as internal below is imported by no external
consumer, so parent AC2 requires it to stay module-private.)*
4. Layering: `worklist.meta.ts` may import format/constants/types;
   `worklist.detail.ts` may import meta/format/constants/types; **no** new cycle
   and no runtime barrel import (AC4).

# Split worklist TUI loop into context and handlers

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 6 of 7 (the hard part).

## Target outcome

`runWorklistTui` (currently lines 5581–7899, ~2,319 lines of nested closures over
one mutable context) becomes a thin orchestrator over named handler modules,
with a **single interface-typed context object owned by one module** and passed
explicitly to handler functions — no state duplication and no class-based
controller rewrite (parent constraint).

## Scope (measured closure groups inside `runWorklistTui`)

| New module | Contents | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.tui-context.ts` | The context interface + factory: `opts`, `termSize`, `items`, `state`, `renderer`, `inputActive`, view flags (`formState`, `preFormMode`, `preHelpMode`, `helpScrollOffset`, `shipItDialog`, `podcastNotice`, `blockedNotice`), freeze/sprint flags, dispose hooks. Single owner of the mutable context (AC5) | ~250 |
| `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` | Pane gate, agent tracker, live event subscriptions, pane-marker apply/refresh/batching, metadata blocker resolution + cache (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8), freeze-state refresh, review-queue sprint state | ~560 |
| `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` | Non-blocking sync status notice (F3 — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N), `cleanup`, `closeEventSubscriber`, `doRefresh` (single-flight + pending), `doSync`, `openShipItDialog` / `openShipItDialogGuarded` | ~480 |
| `worklist.tui-input.ts` | `dispatchMouse`, `handleKeyInput`, streaming stdin decode (`onData` + `KeypressDecoder`), `readKeyFile`/`writeKeyFile`, `buildHelpEntries`/`buildHelpIconLegend` | ~800 |
| `worklist.tui-render.ts` | `render`, `onResize`, `TaskScheduler` wiring, hydrator runner, resume poll, db-change watch, and the `runWorklistTui` orchestrator that constructs the context and registers handlers | ~570 |

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `runWorklistTui` is retained at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical
   signature and return type (`Promise<WorkItem | undefined>`), implemented as a
   thin orchestrator (context construction + handler registration + teardown);
   no module and no single exported function carries the former 2,319-line body
   (AC1).
2. Every new module ≤1,000 lines with a responsibility doc comment; the TUI-local
   sub-banners (metadata-panel dependency blockers — WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8,
   review-queue depth indicator, event-driven window status — WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ,
   non-blocking sync status notice — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N, mouse event dispatch —
   WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ AC2–AC6, streaming stdin decode — WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH,
   consolidated scheduler loop — WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP, hydrator —
   WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI) and their inline work-item ids move verbatim (AC6).
3. **Single context, explicit passing.** The context type is declared once in
   `worklist.tui-context.ts`; handler modules receive it as a parameter and
   never re-declare a mutable field it already owns. `WorkItemListState`
   remains a single instance created by the orchestrator (AC5); the split guard's
   single-owner gate stays green.
4. Lifecycle ordering is preserved exactly: event-subscription setup, pane gate,
   refresh single-flight/pending, scheduler ticks, hydrator, resume poll and
   teardown order are unchanged — verified by the unmodified
   `worklist-integration.test.ts`, `worklist-active-pane-marker.test.ts`,
   `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts`, `worklist-consolidated-refresh.test.ts`,
   `worklist-watch.test.ts`, `worklist-inflight.test.ts`,
   `worklist-sync-notice.test.ts` and `worklist.test.ts` TUI blocks (AC3).
5. Split guard, `tsc --noEmit`/build and the full `packages/herdr` suite pass;
   no new cycle; no runtime barrel import (AC4, AC9).
6. Docs updated: `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block, `onPaneFocused`
   and `isInputActive` references at ~1619 and ~1781, and the ~1829 "task
   registration in `worklist.ts`" note), `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`,
   `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — all path references resolve
   to the new modules.
7. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
   → Owned by this slice: `WorkItemListState` and the extracted TUI context each live in exactly one module and no mutable state is duplicated.

## Minimal implementation

1. Introduce `worklist.tui-context.ts` with the context interface and factory;
   move the `opts`/state/flag declarations into it **without** changing any
   initial value or ordering.
2. Extract `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` (subscriptions, pane markers, blockers,
   freeze/sprint state) as functions taking the context.
3. Extract `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` (`doRefresh`/`doSync`/ship-it dialog/notice/
   cleanup) as functions taking the context.
4. Extract `worklist.tui-input.ts` (`handleKeyInput`/`dispatchMouse`/`onData`/
   key-file IO/help entries) as functions taking the context.
5. Extract `worklist.tui-render.ts` (render/resize/scheduler/hydrator/resume
   poll/db-change watch) and reduce `runWorklistTui` to orchestration.
   Land steps 1–5 as **separate commits**, each with the full suite green, so a
   behavioural regression is attributable to one closure group.
6. Run guard + build + suite; update docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts` — new (single context owner).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-handlers.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-refresh.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-input.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-render.ts` — new (holds the orchestrator).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — re-exports `runWorklistTui`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — consumer; must compile unchanged.
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md` and the five `docs/dev/*` files listed above.

## Constraints

- No class-based controller conversion, no state duplication, no reordering of
  lifecycle steps, no changed defaults or timings.
- The context is interface-typed and passed explicitly; closures may become
  module functions but must not change observable behaviour.
- No barrel/`index.ts` imports inside the new modules; no test edits.

## Dependencies

- `WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J` — refactor guard (test-first).
- `WL-0MVND6DHH008R3LG` — constants/types/layout.
- `WL-0MVND6F9V004IQ3V` — state/navigation.
- `WL-0MVND6H5Q006YO9Z` — presentation.
- `WL-0MVND6J090041GWK` — input pipeline (key/mouse handlers move with it).
- `WL-0MVND6KVF0089878` — renderer/commands (the loop dispatches through them).

## Deliverables

Five TUI modules with a thin `runWorklistTui`, guard + full suite green, docs
updated.

Goal: a local-only pane whose prompt exceeds the local provider's context ceiling should degrade predictably instead of stalling or failing, and the reason should be visible to the operator.

Observed problem: the local provider rejects a local-only request when the projected prompt exceeds ~38k tokens warm, or ~25k on a cold prefix. Because the pane is labelled local-only the proxy refuses the local route, and the work is not processed on the local slot. Evidence in this deployment's route logs (.worklog/local-route.log, 697 turns across 5 roots): 49 turns route remote with fallbackReason resident_prefix_insufficient and 44 with large_context_bypass; 72 turns actually served local. - Is the correct behaviour a fallback to remote for over-threshold requests, an explicit hard error surfaced to the operator, or pre-dispatch routing (choose remote-ok when the projected context exceeds the ceiling)?

- Interaction with WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low priority -> local-only): over-threshold low-priority work must not become unprocessable.

# tree_coverage AC extraction silently ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (`extract_acceptance_criteria`) only collects
markdown bullets that start with `- ` or `+ ` inside the `## Acceptance Criteria`
section. Work items whose ACs are a **numbered** list (`1. …`, `2. …`) yield an
empty AC set, so `run_coverage_review` reports `fully_covered: true` /
`recommendation: proceed` with **zero parent ACs** — the AC coverage gate passes
vacuously instead of verifying that children cover the parent.

Observed during planning of WL-0MVGB23MM004X501: `apply_coverage_review` returned
`action: proceed` with `parent_acs: 0` against a description containing nine
numbered ACs. Contributors have worked around it by manually normalising AC lists
to `- ` bullets (e.g. WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS, WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) or by documenting
the limitation (WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7), which means the failure mode is invisible
unless an operator notices a 0-AC result.

## Desired outcome

1. `extract_acceptance_criteria` also parses numbered list items (`1. `, `1) `)
   inside the AC section, keeping continuation lines and inline code intact.
2. A parent section that has a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading but yields zero
   parsed ACs is reported as a **conflict/stop condition** (or an explicit
   warning in the review result) rather than silently `proceed`, so a silent
   vacuous pass is impossible.
3. Existing bullet-form ACs and all currently passing coverage reviews are
   unaffected (regression tests over both formats).
4. Documentation in the plan/intake skills notes the supported AC formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Numbered AC lists (`1. …`) and bullet lists (`- …`) are both extracted by
  `extract_acceptance_criteria`, with matching output for equivalent content.
- A numbered AC list in a work item description produces a non-zero
  `parent_acs` count from `run_coverage_review`.
- An `## Acceptance Criteria` section that parses to zero ACs no longer returns
  `recommendation: proceed` silently — it is surfaced as a conflict or explicit
  warning in the review result.
- Unit tests cover: numbered list, bullet list, mixed list, empty AC section, and
  the zero-AC stop/warn behaviour.
- Plan and intake skill docs state which AC formats the tooling recognises.

## Notes

- Workaround for items already affected: normalise the AC list to `- ` bullets
  (wording unchanged) so coverage can be computed.

## Problem

The test-run cache (`skill/test_cache.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) can serve a **stale** result, and can also report **missing** for an entry that was just written. Both were observed in one session (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A). Root cause undiagnosed — the symptoms below contradict `compute_git_state`'s documented content-sensitive fingerprint, so the fingerprint itself may be captured at the wrong moment.

Discovered during WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (discovered-from).

**Implementation repository:** the cache code lives in the **SorraAgents** skills repo. This item is tracked in the ContextHub worklog (where it was discovered); all paths below are relative to the SorraAgents repo root.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state()`, `run_cached()`, `lookup()`, `store()`, `query_cached()`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `--scope changed`, `--summary`, `[cached]` marker in non-JSON output
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — existing cache-fingerprint unit tests
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` — existing run_tests cache-integration tests
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — the test-skill cache contract documentation

## Symptom 1 — a stale GREEN was returned for a changed tree

While validating RED witnesses for the peer-offer cooldown work:

1. Production fix applied (5 dirty files) → `run_tests.py --scope changed --group herdr --json` → `Test Files 130 passed`.
2. Production changes reverted (`git checkout -- <3 prod files>`; 2 dirty test files) → the same command → **130 passed / 4007 tests**, i.e. the RED witnesses "passed" without the fix.
3. The same command again, after adding `console.log` diagnostics to those same two test files, **reused the same cache directory** (`metadata.json` `completed_at` unchanged) — a cache hit, despite the file contents having changed.
4. `--no-cache` produced the expected **4 failures**, confirming the RED witnesses were valid.

## Symptom 2 — `--summary` reports `missing` for an entry just stored

Immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full --json` finished green at HEAD (`Test Files 280 passed | 1 skipped`, `Tests 4102 passed | 5 skipped`, cache dir `ada07d39…` with `scope: full`, `test_type: full`, `exit_code: 0`), `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` (with and without `--scope full`) reported `{"scopes":{"all":"missing"}}`. The checkout was clean at the same HEAD; `compute_git_state()` returned `2838fdc3…` while the stored entry held `6155836a…` — so the entry was keyed on a *transient* dirty state that existed during the run (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) and can never be queried again afterwards.

## Verified context (checked while planning, 2026-10-30)

- **Content-sensitive fingerprinting already shipped.** SA-0MVGKZN8C006YNV8 (commit `b51609654`, 2026-10-20) made `compute_git_state()` hash HEAD **plus the content of every path** in `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`. Symptom 1 was observed on 2026-10-26, *after* that fix — so the residual stale hit is **not** the already-fixed content-hash gap; the implementer must reproduce it and find the path that bypasses or mis-times the fingerprint.
- **Symptom 2 has an identified mechanism.** `run_cached()` computes `git_state` **before** the run and stores the entry under that pre-run state, so any transient dirty state at run start (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) keys an entry that a clean checkout at the same HEAD can never query again.
- **The `[cached]` marker already exists** in non-JSON run output (SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY, 2026-08-06), so cache visibility is a regression-guard requirement rather than new behaviour.

## Impact

- A RED/GREEN verification can be silently wrong — exactly the evidence an audit consumes.
- `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate can pass on a stale cached run.
- The audit's `query_cached()` fast path misses for the same reason, forcing an unnecessary full-suite re-execution (F3).
- Agents are likely to trust the green summary and never use `--no-cache`.

## Proposed direction (for intake)

- Make the fingerprint stable for the *state an operator/agent can reproduce*: exclude ignored/transient paths (`.worklog/`, `dist/`, test scratch dirs) from the dirty-path content hash, or snapshot the state before the run rather than after.
- Re-check the content-hash path for `--scope changed` runs (symptom 1) — the file list may be reused where the content hash is not.
- Surface `cached: true` prominently in human-readable output so a re-used result is never mistaken for a fresh one.
- Document/automate: verification runs that must prove RED/GREEN should use `--no-cache`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — Content-only edits invalidate: editing only the contents of an already-modified (dirty) file invalidates the cache entry for that scope/group, proven by a regression test (run A → edit an already-dirty file → run B) that fails against the un-fixed code and passes after the fix.
- AC2 — Post-run queryability: immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full` completes, `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` from a clean checkout at the same HEAD reports the stored entry instead of `missing`, covered by a regression test.
- AC3 — Cache visibility guarded: a cache-served result remains marked `[cached]` in non-JSON output and that marker is covered by a regression test so it cannot silently regress.
- AC4 — Root cause recorded: the mechanism behind each symptom is recorded on this item as a comment before the fix lands, and both regression tests are demonstrated RED against the pre-fix code and GREEN afterwards.
- AC5 — Docs: `skill/test/SKILL.md` states that runs whose result proves RED/GREEN (or supplies evidence an audit consumes) must use `--no-cache`.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Changing the cache key/namespace model (tree fingerprints, worktree/main-checkout unification) — tracked by SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB and SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V. This item must not duplicate or block those.

## Risky assumptions

- The residual stale hit (symptom 1) is fixable without changing the fingerprint contract. If reproduction shows it needs the tree-fingerprint binding, stop, record the finding on SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB, and re-scope this item instead of expanding it.
- `--scope changed` runs are keyed per-command through `run_cached()`, so a content edit must change the key; if it does not, the defect is in the changed-scope command/file-list derivation rather than in the fingerprint.

## Related work

- SA-0MVGKZN8C006YNV8 (completed) — content-based git-state fingerprint; partial overlap with AC1's original premise.
- SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB (blocked) — tree-fingerprint cache binding for the finish gate.
- SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V (open) — unify the test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout.
- WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (completed) — discovery session.

## OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking)

- OPEN QUESTION for the producer: AC3 keeps today's per-suite `[cached]` marker; is that enough of a signal, or should a cached run also be surfaced at the run/JSON summary level (e.g. `cached_suites`)? Non-blocking — AC3 guards existing behaviour with a test either way.
- OPEN QUESTION for the producer: should the symptom-2 fix also make previously orphaned entries discoverable (re-key on demand), or is preventing orphaned entries (store under a state the operator can reproduce) sufficient? Non-blocking — AC2 only requires that newly stored entries are queryable.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/package.json` declares a root `bin` entry
(`worklog-pane-close` -> `dist/pane-close-cli.js`) and a `postinstall` script,
but the committed `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` (last touched
2026-08-11, WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4) predates both. Any `npm ci`/`npm install` in
that package rewrites the lockfile with `hasInstallScript: true` and the root
`bin` block.

`tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` executes `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
(cwd = repo root), which runs `npm ci` inside `packages/herdr`. The rewritten
lockfile is therefore a mutation of a guarded checkout made during a test run,
so the test skill's live-repo guard fails the run:

```
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for <repo>.
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/package-lock.json
```

Every test in the suite passes (281 files / 4,113 tests, exit 0) — only the run
verdict is failed. Consequences:

- The per-repo test cache can never hold a green full-suite entry for HEAD, so
  the audit skill cannot auto-verify execution-dependent ACs (F3 re-executes and
  fails the same way).
- Each full-suite run leaves the main checkout dirty.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` is regenerated (`npm install` in
   `packages/herdr`) and committed so it matches `package.json`'s `bin` and
   `postinstall`.
2. A full-suite run (`run_tests.py --scope full`) at that commit reports
   `success: true` with no `live_repo_mutation` field, and leaves
   `git status` clean.
3. `npm run build` and `npm ci` in `packages/herdr` produce no further lockfile
   diff.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/package-lock.json`
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — read-only
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` — read-only (reproduction)

## Goal

**As** an operator running several worklog roots on one machine, **I want** the downtime leader to know about a root even when no herdr instance happens to be running in it, **so that** a root with dispatchable work is never invisible to the dispatcher.

## Problem

The dispatcher's candidate universe is derived from **live instances**, not registered roots:

- `computeMostImportantItem` runs per instance and is called by `runCoordinationCheckIn`; only a running herdr instance in a root writes a coordination entry (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts:145`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:928+`).
- The leader's only cross-root reach is the offer list plus one own-backlog fallback hard-scoped to `opts.cwd` (`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:801-880`, AC2 of WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24).

Measured 2026-10-27T21:55Z: `ContextHub` has **9 of 30** window items dispatchable (`WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ`, `WL-0MNM7EVJG0097Y44`, `WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND`, six refactor items, …), and **zero** coordination entries, because no herdr instance is running in that root. Its per-worklog `downtime-coordination.json` is `{"version":1,"entries":[]}`. The machine-wide file holds only `tce-the-rising` entries.

Leadership rotation cannot fix this: the empty-leader hand-off (`WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A`) hands off to *a peer*, and there is no peer in that root to hand off to.

## Why this is separate from `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V`

It is a different problem class — **root discovery**, not dispatcher gating. Fixing the audit-tier budget or adding attribution would not make a root with no open pane reachable. Conversely, a root sweep would not have fixed `AI_Hell` (all items held) or `tce-the-rising` (audit tier unreachable).

## Options (to evaluate at intake)

- **O1 — Registered roots.** An explicit config list (e.g. `downtimeWorklogRoots`), or discovery by scanning a parent directory for `.worklog/worklog.db`. The leader sweeps registered roots round-robin via `getHerdrListHead(root, window)` and applies the same sequential filter chain. Note `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` still exists with a cursor (the retired-by-WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 helpers), so the cursor machinery is partly present.
- **O2 — Per-root offers from a single instance.** One instance offers on behalf of a set of roots. Cheaper than O1 but reintroduces "who offers which root" ownership questions.
- **O3 — Hardware/heartbeat registry.** Instances publish liveness per root so the leader can distinguish "no instance" from "instance offered nothing". Overlaps with the stale-entry problem (see below).

## Related observation

Coordination entries never expire: `pruneStaleEntries` is a deliberate no-op (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts:366`, WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P), and `hasPeerOffer` (`coordination.ts:350`) only checks `instanceId !== self && workItemId.length > 0`. During the 2026-10-27 investigation the dead instance `b4365ff1` (lastUpdated `2026-10-27T14:30:20Z`, 7+ hours stale) still counted as a live peer. The predicate is documented as "conservative… never a starvation", which was sound when entries expired; with expiry retired it no longer is. Any solution here should also decide whether a stale entry should make the leader *more* willing to sweep.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A root with dispatchable work but **no running herdr instance** is reachable by the leader, and work from it is dispatched. Verified live on `ContextHub` (currently 9 dispatchable, 0 offers).
- AC2: `AI_Hell`-style gated roots are still not dispatched — a sweep must not bypass any existing safety gate (`assignee` hold, producer-review, code-freeze, freshness, caps, slot minimums, in-flight, review-queue). Gates remain sequential filters.
- AC3: The canonical ranking contract is preserved: a sweep is a bounded **window** over registered roots using the same `getHerdrListHead` path, never a second ranking.
- AC4: Fairness: no single root can monopolise the leader (a bounded per-root share or round-robin cursor), demonstrated by a multi-root test with two roots each holding dispatchable work.
- AC5: Fail-open: an unreadable/missing root in the registry is skipped without a strike, and never crashes the tick.
- AC6: Fail-safe: an empty or unresolvable registry leaves today's behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged.
- AC7: The stale-coordination-entry question above is explicitly resolved (either entries gain a heartbeat, or `hasPeerOffer` is made liveness-aware) with the decision recorded on this item.
- AC8: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the root-discovery model and how it composes with the offer list.

## Constraints

- Must not reinstate the unconditional non-critical window widening superseded by WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9.
- Must not require a running pane per root (that is the bug being fixed).
- Config schema additions need clamping/validation consistent with `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.

- **`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parsers.ts`** — `parseAuditCandidateScopeOutput(stdout)`: leaf **only** for a present-and-empty `children` array; `'parent'` for a non-empty array; `{ok:false}` for malformed JSON, the CLI's `{success:false,error}` not-found body (which exits 0 — checked explicitly), absent/non-array `children`, missing `workItem`, or a **non-root candidate** (non-empty `parentId`; the audit tier is `--root-only`). - **`downtime-worker.worker-contract.ts`** — `getAuditCandidateScope` is now **required** (C1 declared it optional; C2 wires the real implementation, so no deps object can silently skip the fail-closed lookup). The `makeDeps` neutral `{ok:true, scope:'parent'}` default is unchanged.

The parser spells its result `{ok:true; scope:'leaf'|'parent'} | {ok:false}` instead of importing `AuditCandidateScopeResult` from `downtime-worker.gates.ts`: `gates → selection → parsers` already exists, so a `parsers → gates` type edge closes a **new split-family cycle** the frozen guard rejects (observed red: `adds no import cycle outside the recorded baseline` → `[gates, parsers, selection]`). - `npx tsc -p packages/herdr/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → clean.
- `npx tsx scripts/check-mock-budget.ts` → `Mock budget OK`.

"Audit-tier selection … fetches the candidate's children (`wl show <id> --children --json`; fail-closed → treat as parent, all-slots gate)." — delivered by this dep + the parse-to-`{ok:false}` mapping + `classifyAuditScope`'s `{ok:false} → 'parent'` default (C1 suite) and the new dep-level fail-closed tests in `index.test.ts`.
